entries.lesson_core_move: Interpret |$H(j\omega)$| as the frequency-dependent amplitude scaling applied by a continuous-time LTI system to sinusoidal inputs, using its variation over $\omega$ to identify which components are attenuated, passed, or amplified.

images.section_title: Interpreting a Magnitude-Response Curve Across Frequency
images.image_description: A clean instructional line plot of $|H(j\omega)|$ versus $\omega$ with a bold horizontal reference line at $|H(j\omega)|=1$. Draw one continuous magnitude-response curve that sits above 1 over a low-frequency band, stays near 1 over a middle band, and falls below 1 over a high-frequency band. Label the horizontal axis with $\omega$ and the vertical axis with $|H(j\omega)|$. Optionally mark one representative frequency in each band so the viewer can read the above, equal, and below-1 regions directly.
images.report: Decreasing magnitude-response curve with low-frequency and high-frequency end markers.; Unity reference line at |$H(jω)$|=1.; Low/high labels placed below the x-axis.

entries.lesson_core_move: Classify a filter's passband behavior from its magnitude response by comparing low- and high-frequency gain to decide whether the LTI system is low-pass, high-pass, or neither.

images.section_title: Introduction to Filter Interpretation from Magnitude Response
images.image_description: A clean magnitude-response plot of $|H(j\omega)|$ versus $\omega$ with the low-frequency and high-frequency ends highlighted and a unity line at $|H(j\omega)|=1$. Horizontal axis labeled $\omega$, vertical axis labeled $|H(j\omega)|$, unity reference line at $|H(j\omega)|=1$, highlighted low-frequency end, highlighted high-frequency end, and a simple gain curve. Keep the graph uncluttered and instructional so the low-vs-high comparison is obvious at a glance.
images.report: Magnitude-response curve with a solid unity reference line.; Low and high end markers use dotted guides and $\omega$ labels.
images.lesson_core_move: Classify a filter's passband behavior from its magnitude response by comparing low- and high-frequency gain to decide whether the LTI system is low-pass, high-pass, or neither.

images.section_title: Reading Low- and High-Frequency Gain from a Magnitude Response
images.image_description: Create a clean magnitude-response plot with horizontal axis labeled $\omega$ and vertical axis labeled $|H(j\omega)|$. Draw a unity reference line at $|H(j\omega)|=1$. Show a simple decreasing curve with a low-frequency plateau around 1.6 on the left and a high-frequency plateau around 0.35 on the right. Mark the left end as the low-frequency side and the right end as the high-frequency side. Keep the plot uncluttered and make the two end heights easy to compare.
images.report: Decreasing magnitude-response curve with a high low-frequency plateau and low high-frequency plateau.; Endpoint markers and the unity line support the comparison in the question prompt.
images.lesson_core_move: Classify a filter's passband behavior from its magnitude response by comparing low- and high-frequency gain to decide whether the LTI system is low-pass, high-pass, or neither.

images.section_title: Reading Low- and High-Frequency Gain from a Magnitude Response
images.image_description: Create a clean magnitude-response plot with horizontal axis labeled $\omega$ and vertical axis labeled $|H(j\omega)|$. Draw a unity reference line at $|H(j\omega)|=1$. Mark the left end as the low-frequency side and the right end as the high-frequency side. Keep the plot uncluttered and make the two end heights easy to compare.
images.report: Increasing magnitude-response curve with a sub-unity low end and a super-unity high end.; Endpoint markers make the low-vs-high comparison immediate.

images.section_title: Reading Low- and High-Frequency Gain from a Magnitude Response
images.image_description: A magnitude-response plot with a visible low-frequency plateau around 1.5 and a high-frequency plateau around 0.4, plus a unity line at $|H(j\omega)|=1$. The horizontal axis is labeled $\omega$, the vertical axis is labeled $|H(j\omega)|$, and the curve is simple and uncluttered so the low-frequency end and high-frequency end are easy to compare at a glance.
images.report: Tutorial example with a clear downward gain trend across frequency.; Unity line and endpoint markers emphasize the end-behavior comparison.

images.section_title: Classifying a Low-Pass Filter from Magnitude Response
images.image_description: A clean magnitude-response plot with horizontal axis labeled $\omega$ and vertical axis labeled $|H(j\omega)|$. Include a unity reference line at $|H(j\omega)|=1$. The curve starts clearly above 1 at the low-frequency end, ends clearly below 1 at the high-frequency end, and slopes smoothly downward across the plot. Keep the graph uncluttered and omit any phase information or extra panels.
images.report: Low-pass example with low-frequency gain above unity and high-frequency gain below unity.; Smooth downward transition with marked low and high ends.
images.lesson_core_move: Classify a filter's passband behavior from its magnitude response by comparing low- and high-frequency gain to decide whether the LTI system is low-pass, high-pass, or neither.

images.section_title: Classifying a Low-Pass Filter from Magnitude Response
images.image_description: A clean magnitude-response plot with horizontal axis labeled $\omega$ and vertical axis labeled $|H(j\omega)|$. Include a unity reference line at $|H(j\omega)|=1$. The low-frequency end is around 0.8, the high-frequency end is around 0.2, and the curve slopes smoothly downward so the low-frequency end is still visibly higher than the high-frequency end. Keep the graph uncluttered and omit any phase information or extra panels.
images.report: Low-pass example with both ends below unity but a higher low-frequency end than high-frequency end.; The curve stays below the unity line across the band.
images.lesson_core_move: Classify a filter's passband behavior from its magnitude response by comparing low- and high-frequency gain to decide whether the LTI system is low-pass, high-pass, or neither.

images.section_title: Classifying a Low-Pass Filter from Magnitude Response
images.image_description: A magnitude-response plot with horizontal axis labeled $\omega$ and vertical axis labeled $|H(j\omega)|$. images.report: Tutorial low-pass example with a clearly stronger low-frequency end.; Dotted guides and $\omega$ labels show the two ends being compared.
images.lesson_core_move: Classify a filter's passband behavior from its magnitude response by comparing low- and high-frequency gain to decide whether the LTI system is low-pass, high-pass, or neither.

images.image_description: A magnitude-response plot with horizontal axis labeled $\omega$ and vertical axis labeled $|H(j\omega)|$. The low-frequency end is clearly below the unity reference line at $|H(j\omega)|=1$, the high-frequency end is clearly above it, and the curve makes a smooth upward transition between the ends. images.section_title: Classifying Neither Low-Pass Nor High-Pass Behavior
images.image_description: A clean magnitude-response plot of $|H(j\omega)|$ versus $\omega$ with the low- and high-frequency ends both around 0.6, clearly below the unity line at $|H(j\omega)|=1$, while the middle region rises above 1 into a hump. images.image_description: A clean magnitude-response plot of $|H(j\omega)|$ versus $\omega$ with the low- and high-frequency ends both around 1.4, clearly above the unity line at $|H(j\omega)|=1$, while the middle region dips below 1 into a notch. images.image_description: A magnitude-response plot with horizontal axis labeled $\omega$ and vertical axis labeled $|H(j\omega)|$. The middle region rises into a clear hump above 1, so the response is not low-pass or high-pass. Keep the plot uncluttered and omit any phase information or extra panels.
